claim: Gardens by the Bay 2026 prices: two conservatories S$46 non-resident adult; outdoor gardens free; both domes must be visited same day; Supertree Observatory ~S$14, closed 11 Jun 2026.
quote: The combined entry fee for adults for the Cloud Forest and Flower Dome is SGD 46... Visits to both Conservatories must be completed on the same day. The Supertree Observatory will be closed on 11 June 2026 for maintenance.

claim: Cloud Forest houses a 35 m indoor waterfall in a misty mountain, with Avatar: The Experience zones.
quote: Cloud Forest features life-sized dinosaurs in Jurassic World The Experience... the world's tallest indoor waterfall at 35 metres.

claim: Flower Dome shows seasonal floral displays including Tulipmania 24 Apr–17 May 2026.
quote: Flower Dome offers gardens with baobabs, olive trees, and vibrant seasonal floral displays, including Tulipmania 2026 running from April 24 to May 17, 2026.

claim: Garden Rhapsody is free at Supertree Grove 19:45 & 20:45; Spectra is free at MBS 20:00/21:00 daily plus 22:00 Fri-Sat.
quote: The 15-minute show plays at 7.45 pm and 8.45 pm daily, and is free... Spectra shows are free daily at 8pm and 9pm on Sunday to Thursday; and at 8pm, 9pm, and 10pm on Friday and Saturday.

claim: Garden Rhapsody is the free nightly light-and-sound show at Supertree Grove.
quote: Garden Rhapsody - Singapore

claim: MBS SkyPark Observation Deck sits ~200 m up for skyline views; timed entry.
quote: SkyPark Observation Deck | Attractions in Singapore | Marina Bay Sands

claim: SkyPark 2026 adult ticket S$35 non-peak, S$39 peak (sunset); tickets are timed.
quote: non-peak tickets are Adult S$35... peak tickets are Adult S$39... SkyPark tickets are timed, so you must select a specific entry time when booking.

claim: Spectra is a free nightly outdoor light-and-water show at the MBS Event Plaza.
quote: Spectra is a free, nightly outdoor 15-minute extravaganza displayed over the water at the Event Plaza.

claim: Merlion Park is free and open 24/7; best photographed before 9am or after 7pm; framed against Marina Bay Sands.
quote: Merlion Park is open 24/7 free of charge... best visited before 9am or after 7pm for thinner crowds and better light.

claim: The Merlion statue stands 8.6 m tall, built 1972 by Lim Nang Seng.
quote: The Merlion is a mythical creature... standing 8.6 meters tall... Crafted from cement mortar in 1972 by local sculptor Lim Nang Seng.

claim: The HSBC Rain Vortex at Jewel Changi is the world's tallest indoor waterfall at 40 m and is free to view.
quote: The HSBC Rain Vortex at Jewel Changi Airport is the world's tallest indoor waterfall at 40 metres — and viewing it is completely free.

claim: Most of Jewel is free (Rain Vortex, Forest Valley, Level 5); a nightly light show runs from 20:00; only Canopy Park play attractions are ticketed.
quote: Most of Jewel is completely free to explore... A nightly Light & Music Showcase runs on the waterfall from 8pm... Canopy Park (Paid Attractions).

claim: Canopy Park (Level 5) is ticketed and includes the 23 m Mastercard Canopy Bridge over the Rain Vortex, mazes and slides.
quote: a suspension bridge called the Mastercard Canopy Bridge, located 23 metres above the ground and offering a panoramic view of the Rain Vortex.

claim: Singapore Botanic Gardens is free and open 05:00 to midnight daily, except the National Orchid Garden.
quote: The Gardens is open from 5 a.m. to 12 midnight daily and entry is free, except for the National Orchid Garden.

claim: Singapore Botanic Gardens was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2015 — the first tropical and Singapore's only such site.
quote: inscription occurring on 4 July 2015... Singapore Botanic Gardens is the first tropical, and only the third botanic gardens on the UNESCO World Heritage listing.

claim: The National Orchid Garden holds over 60,000 orchids, one of the world's largest tropical orchid displays.
quote: The National Orchid Garden is home to over 60,000 orchids and has one of the world's largest tropical orchid displays.

claim: National Orchid Garden 2026 adult admission is about S$5.
quote: the National Orchid Garden requires paid admission at SGD 5 for adults in 2026.

claim: Singapore Flyer is a 165 m observation wheel with a 30-minute rotation in glass capsules.
quote: The Singapore Flyer is a 165 metre tall ferris wheel, and visitors are transported on a 30-minute journey in glass capsules.

claim: Singapore Flyer adult S$40 vs MBS SkyPark S$35; SkyPark is higher, open-air and you can stay as long as you like, so it wins for first-timers.
quote: Singapore Flyer tickets cost 40 SGD for an adult, while tickets for the Marina Bay Sands SkyPark... cost 35 SGD... You can stay at SkyPark as long as you like (while the flyer is 30 min).

claim: ArtScience Museum's teamLab Future World needs a timed-entry ticket; selected zones unavailable 15 Jun–28 Aug 2026.
quote: a timed entry ticket is required... selected areas will be temporarily unavailable from 15 Jun to 28 Aug 2026 as enhancements take place.

claim: ArtScience Museum admission runs roughly S$23 (around US$23) for adults.
quote: reference adult ticket prices around $23 USD... All prices include admission to the ArtScience Museum.

claim: National Gallery Singapore tickets ~S$14–20; it sits between City Hall and the former Supreme Court; Supreme Court wing galleries close from 1 Apr 2026.
quote: National Gallery Singapore Tickets 2026 S$18.00... From 1 April 2026, all galleries on Levels 3, 4 and 5 of the Former Supreme Court Wing will be closed.

claim: The Civic District concentrates colonial sights — City Hall, old Supreme Court, National Gallery, Raffles Hotel, St Andrew's Cathedral (free, 9-16:00).
quote: The Civic District houses many of Singapore's top historical and cultural sights... St Andrew's Cathedral is open 9am-4pm and is free to visit.

claim: Raffles Hotel is a preserved colonial landmark in the civic district, free to walk through.
quote: a beacon of classic colonial architecture perfectly preserved among our modern-skyscraper neighbours.

claim: Buddha Tooth Relic Temple in Chinatown is a five-storey temple with free entry, near Sri Mariamman Temple.
quote: Buddha Tooth Relic Temple & Museum in Singapore... within comfortable walking distance of Sri Mariamman Temple.

claim: Buddha Tooth Relic Temple is free, open daily 07:00-19:00, with a modest dress code (shoulders and knees covered; sarongs lent).
quote: Admission is free... open daily from 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM... No sleeveless tops... Shoulders and knees must be covered... sarongs are available at the entrance.

claim: Thian Hock Keng is Singapore's oldest Chinese (Hokkien) temple, dedicated to sea-goddess Mazu.
quote: Thian Hock Keng Temple | Oldest Chinese Temple in Singapore... dedicated to Mazu, a Chinese sea goddess.

claim: Thian Hock Keng (1839-42) was built without nails and is free to enter; the Chinatown Heritage Centre is at 48 Pagoda St.
quote: the entire structure assembled without nails... you don't need a ticket to enter. The Chinatown Heritage Centre is located at 48 Pagoda Street.

claim: Little India's sights include Tekka Centre wet market and the colourful Tan Teng Niah villa.
quote: Stroll through the Tekka Centre hawkers market... Admire the Tan Teng Niah, a colorful Chinese villa in Little India.

claim: Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple (Serangoon Rd) is dedicated to Kali with an ornate gopuram; free, open ~08:00-12:00 & 16:00-21:00, modest dress.
quote: the Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple is believed to be the first Hindu temple in Singapore to be dedicated to the Hindu Goddess Kali... free entry, respectful dress.

claim: Kampong Glam's top sights are the Sultan Mosque, Arab Street and Haji Lane; visit ~08:00 for empty streets.
quote: The top must-see sites are the Sultan Mosque (Gold Dome), Haji Lane Murals... Visit at 8:00 AM for empty streets/photography.

claim: Sultan Mosque is free with a modest dress code (shoulders/knees covered; free robes lent); avoid Friday 11:00-14:00 prayers.
quote: dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered)... the mosque provides free robes at the entrance... Avoid Fridays between 11 AM and 2 PM.

claim: Tiong Bahru is Singapore's first public-housing estate (1936-41), an Art Deco quarter with rounded corners and three Yip Yew Chong heritage murals.
quote: Built by the Singapore Improvement Trust between 1936 and 1941... iconic rounded corners... three murals in Tiong Bahru painted by Yip Yew Chong.

claim: Hell's Museum at Haw Par Villa is S$20 adult / S$10 kid (under-6 free), 10:00-18:00; park partially closed for works from 8 Dec 2025 but Museum stays open.
quote: Hell's Museum tickets cost SG$20 for adults and SG$10 for kids... Haw Par Villa is temporarily partially closed... from 8 December 2025, though Hell's Museum... will remain open.

claim: Haw Par Villa itself is free, an outdoor park of 1,000+ statues and 150 dioramas of Chinese folklore.
quote: entry to Haw Par Villa itself is free... over 1,000 statues and 150 dioramas depicting Chinese folklore and mythology.

claim: The Southern Ridges is a ~10 km elevated trail connecting four parks including Mount Faber and Telok Blangah Hill.
quote: The Southern Ridges comprises one of the most stunning hiking trails in Singapore, spanning a total length of 10km and connecting 4 parks.

claim: Henderson Waves is Singapore's highest pedestrian bridge at 36 m, free to walk, with panoramic city views.
quote: Standing 36 meters above Henderson Road... the highest pedestrian bridge in Singapore offering breathtaking panoramic views.

claim: MacRitchie TreeTop Walk is a free 250 m canopy-level suspension bridge; best in early morning to avoid heat.
quote: The TreeTop Walk is a 250-metre free-standing suspension bridge at canopy level between two ridges, and admission is totally FREE.

claim: TreeTop Walk is open Tue-Fri 09:00-17:00, Sat-Sun/PH 08:30-17:00, closed Mondays.
quote: Opening hours are Tue-Fri 9am-5pm and Sat-Sun & PH 8.30am-5pm (Closed on Mondays).

claim: Pulau Ubin holds Singapore's last kampong; the bumboat from Changi Point costs ~S$4 each way and departs once 12 passengers board.
quote: The 10-minute journey typically costs $4 per person each way... departing when there are 12 passengers on board.

claim: Pulau Ubin is an NParks-managed island reachable by bumboat from Changi Point Ferry Terminal.
quote: Visit Pulau Ubin

claim: Pulau Ubin's Chek Jawa wetlands has a boardwalk and Jejawi Tower; the guided pontoon tour is suspended early 2026 but boardwalks stay open 07:00-19:00.
quote: the Chek Jawa Wetlands guided tour is suspended due to maintenance... The boardwalks, Jejawi Tower, and Visitor Centre remain open from 7 AM to 7 PM daily.

claim: Sentosa offers free sights and a free beach shuttle tram serving Palawan, Siloso and Tanjong beaches.
quote: Sentosa Beach Shuttle is a free-to-ride tram that serves Palawan Beach, Siloso Beach, and Tanjong Beach.

claim: Sentosa's Fort Siloso Skywalk is free; Palawan Beach has a suspension bridge to the 'southernmost point of continental Asia'.
quote: The Fort Siloso Skywalk is free and you go up via lift... a suspension bridge that leads to a small islet... said to be the southernmost point of continental Asia.

claim: Singapore Cable Car round-trip Sky Pass is S$35 adult (both Mount Faber and Sentosa lines), offering a 360° harbour view.
quote: A round-trip Sky Pass for an adult costs S$35... access to all six stations across both lines.

claim: The cable car links Mount Faber to Sentosa with aerial skyline views.
quote: Singapore Cable Car: Scenic Rides & Tickets in Sentosa

claim: Lazarus Island (quiet beach) is reached by ferry to St John's Island then a causeway walk; book ahead on busy weekends.
quote: Lazarus Island is part of Singapore's Southern Islands, connected to St. John's Island by a short causeway... one of Singapore's secret beaches.

claim: Best weather is roughly Feb-Apr and Jun-Sep; the wet NE monsoon Nov-Jan brings ~19 rain days/month in short evening storms.
quote: the dry season... February to October... The rainy season in Singapore is from November to January... averaging 19 rainy days in November/December.
